items.article: America may finally have a plan to survive the demise of the penny. America may finally have a plan to survive without pennies. The Treasury Department stopped minting pennies in 2025, under orders from President Donald Trump . Pennies cost more to mint than they were worth. Most Americans found them a nuisance. But retailers need pennies to make change, and penny shortages vexed cashiers even before production ceased. With the penny tray empty, how can a clerk settle a $9.98 transaction when the customer pays with a ten-dollar bill? This week, Congress passed a bill that could solve the penny problem. The Common Cents Act , approved by the Senate on Sept. 28, permits retailers to round cash transactions to the nearest five cents when neither buyer nor seller has exact change. The guidance sounds simple enough, but some states and cities have laws that forbid retailers to “round.” The Common Cents Act would effectively overrule them. “It’s meant to eliminate those awkward situations where, if you buy something for 99 cents and you hand over a dollar bill, the retailer doesn’t give you anything back because they don’t have pennies,” said Steve Kenneally, senior vice president for payments at the American Bankers Association.

NPS Sanchay is designed to simplify retirement savings, with a predefined investment approach and flexible contribution options. Here’s who can apply and how the scheme works. The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority ( PFRDA ) has announced the NPS Sanchay Pension Yatra on NPS Diwas 2026, a pension-awareness initiative that will be held across four cities from 1 October to 16 October 2026. In an X post, PFRDA said, “Whether your income is high or low, preparing for a secure future is essential for everyone. Through the NPS Sanchay Pension Yatra, pension awareness is being extended to various cities across the country.” The pension awareness drive will be held from 1 October to 16 October 2026 across Delhi, Ahmedabad, Bengaluru and Kolkata. The Yatra aims to raise awareness about retirement savings and NPS Sanchay among people. Here's what you need to know about the NPS Sanchay scheme. NPS Sanchay is a retirement-focused scheme under the All Citizen Model and Multiple Scheme Framework (MSF) of the National Pension System (NPS), aimed at people working in the informal sector. It was introduced on 6 May 2026. It is designed to make retirement investing simpler for people who may not have extensive knowledge or investment experience.
